messages:
Samir: Quick sync 1 PRs diverging on tool-calling output examples: always-envelope vs compact-when-parsed. Which do we canonicalize in tutorials?
Maria Chen: Compact in tutorials for readability. Add an interoperability section that documents envelope + migration steps.
Jake L: Agree. Show compact in starter guides, envelope in advanced/compat. Add pseudo-code for fallback.
Olivia P: I'll patch broken links to the archived invoke page and rename the API flag instances from `compact_response` to `compact_mode`.
Samir: Proposed pseudo-code: `if parse_success: return parsed_obj else: return {"tool_name": t, "raw": raw_string}`. Use raw as a string in examples to avoid nested assumptions.
Maria Chen: I'll write the Python snippet handling both shapes and include a small unit-test example `assert parse(e) or fallback(e)`. Also add a truncated/streaming example to show fallback.
Jake L: I'll add a TypeScript snippet and update the samples index to point to both snippets + migration guide. Also include a one-liner metric for monitoring: `parse_fail_rate = failed_parses / total_calls`.
docs-bot: Reminder: docs PR #4821 mentions the old flag and will need rebasing.
Olivia P: PR checklist: update internal anchors, run S/R for flag rename, and replace links to archived invoke page. Tagging @docs-owners for review.
Samir: Owners: Maria (Python + migration note), Jake (TS + index), Olivia (linkfix + flag rename), Samir (compat paragraph + envelope example). Goal: thin PRs by EOD tomorrow. After PRs land I'll collate a release-note blurb. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
